projects.name: Millbrae and Burlingame Shoreline Resilience Project (MBSRP)
projects.admin_region: San Francisco Bay Adaptation, Todd Hallenbeck, Bay Conservation and Development Commission
projects.abstract: The Millbrae and Burlingame Shoreline Resilience Project (MBSRP) will provide long-term climate resilience against sea level rise and extreme storms for developed, natural, and public access areas. The main areas of focus of this project are coastal flood protection, public access and recreation, and habitat.
projects.cost_basis: Funding allocated to the planning phase: $4.0M of the Coastal Conservancy grant + $300,000 FEMA BRIC (Burlingame; $200,000 OneShoreline match)

projects.name: Redwood Shores Sea Level Rise Protection Project
projects.admin_region: San Francisco Bay Adaptation, Todd Hallenbeck, Bay Conservation and Development Commission
projects.abstract: The project aims to modify the levee system around Redwood Shores to become eligible for accreditation by FEMA, avoid properties in the area being designated as a Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA), and establish long-term resilience against sea level rise that benefits the region.
projects.cost_basis: Up-front cost estimates for the two 60% design alternatives: ~$440M wider levee (Alt 1), ~$324M floodwalls on existing levee (Alt 2); from the Aug 2026 City Council item, as quoted
projects.cost_source: Sierra Club Loma Prieta, Two 60 Percent Design Alternatives (Aug 2026) https://www.sierraclub.org/loma-prieta/two-60-percent-design-alternatives-redwood-shores-sea-level-rise-protection-project
projects.notes: Read from the EcoAtlas project page on Nov 5, 2026.
